title: Definition
head: environment
name: Irreducible holomorphic eta quotients

title: Theorem A
body_md: There are only finitely many irreducible holomorphic eta quotients of a given level.
head: environment

title: Theorem B
body_md: For an integer $k\geq 2$, the levels of the factors of a holomorphic eta quotient $f$ of level $N$ and weight $k/2$ divide $\operatorname{lcm}(N, \mathcal{M}_{k-1}).$
head: environment

title: Corollary~C
body_md: The levels of the factors of a holomorphic eta quotient of weight $1$ and level $N$ divide $\operatorname{lcm}(N, 12)$.
head: environment

title: Theorem D
body_md:
Let $f$ be a reducible holomorphic eta quotient  of level $N>1$  and
let $M$ be the minimum of the 
levels  of the proper factors of $f$. Then each prime
divisor of $M$  also divides $N$ and 
$$M<N^{2^{O(N^{2+\varepsilon})}},$$
where the implied 
constant is effectively computable.
head: environment

title: Theorem E
body_md:
Each reducible holomorphic eta quotient of a prime power level $N$ has a proper factor whose level divides $N$. 
\hypertarget{E}{\color{white}{E}}
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
\textnormal{A holomorphic eta quotient on $\Gamma_0(N)$ is called axial
if it vanishes only at a single cusp class 
of $\Gamma_0(N)$.
Else, it is called a generic holomorphic eta quotient on $\Gamma_0(N)$. If an eta quotient $f$ on $\Gamma_0(N)$ vanishes at all the cusps of $\Gamma_0(N)$, then $f$ is called a cuspidal eta quotient.}
head: environment
name: \emph{Axial, generic and cuspidal eta quotients

label: 12:00PM
title: Definition
head: environment
name: Special set of cusp classes

label: sth
title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $S_N$ be a special set of cusp classes of $\Gamma_0(N)$. 
Each generic holomorphic eta quotient on $\Gamma_0(N)$ which is not factorizable on $\Gamma_0(N)$
is uniquely identified by its orders of vanishing at the cusp classes in $S_N$.
\label{sth}
head: environment

label: 17:02PM
title: Corollary
body_md:
A generic irreducible holomorphic eta quotient\footnote{In particular, each irreducible cuspidal eta quotient on $\Gamma_0(N)$ is uniquely identified by its orders of vanishing at only
$\lfloor2(\log_2 N)^{r-1}\rfloor$ cusps of $\Gamma_0(N)$.} on $\Gamma_0(N)$ 
is uniquely identified by its orders of vanishing at only
$\lfloor2(\log_2 N)^{r-1}\rfloor$ cusps
of $\Gamma_0(N)$, where 
$r$ denotes the number of distinct prime divisors of $N$.
\label{17:02PM}
head: environment

label: ppi
title: Corollary
head: environment

label: a-l
title: Corollary
body_md:
A generic irreducible holomorphic eta quotient 
which is also an Atkin-Lehner eigenform of level $N={\prod_{p|N}}p^{n_p}$,
is uniquely determined by its orders of vanishing at only
$$\underset{p|N}{\prod}\left\lceil\frac{(n_p+1)}2\right\rceil-\underset{p|N}{\prod}\left\lceil\frac{(n_p-1)}2\right\rceil$$
cusps of $\Gamma_0(N)$. 
\label{a-l}
head: environment

label: fi
title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $f$ be a generic irreducible holomorphic eta quotient and a Fricke eigenform
of a prime power level. Then $f$ is uniquely determined by its order of vanishing
at $\infty$.
\label{fi}

body_md:
For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a primitive and irreducible 
cuspidal eta quotient 
of weight $k/2$ and level $2^{2k}$, viz. $\mathcal{H}_{2,2k}$.

title: Corollary
body_md:
Except for the cases in \eqref{redH}, the following assertions hold:

\noindent
 $(a)$ All the rescalings of $\mathcal{H}_{p,n}$ are irreducible.\\ 
  $(b)$ All the images of $\mathcal{H}_{p,n}$ under Atkin-Lehner involutions are irreducible.\\
$(c)$ All the rescalings of the images of $\mathcal{H}_{p,n}$ under Atkin-Lehner involutions are irreducible.\\
$(d)$ All the images under Atkin-Lehner involutions of the rescalings\footnote{Atkin-Lehner involutions and rescalings do not commute with each other in general.} 
 of $\mathcal{H}_{p,n}$ are irreducible.\\
$(e)$ Under every arbitray finite sequence of compositions of Atkin-Lehner involutions and rescalings, the image of $\mathcal{H}_{p,n}$ 
is irreducbile.
\label{cor2}
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
$(a)$ 
     
Holomorphy and cuspidality of eta quotients are preserved by
Atkin-Lehner involutions.
             
                                                                                                   
\newline$(b)$ Let $u$ be a unitary divisor of $N$. For eta quotients $f,g$ and $h$ on $\Gamma_0(N)$, we have 
$f=gh$ if and only if $$\mathcal{AL}_{u,N}(f)=\mathcal{AL}_{u,N}(g)\times\mathcal{AL}_{u,N}(h).$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
\label{7:03PM}

label: b2
title: Lemma
body_md:
For $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $B_N\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_N\times\mathbb{D}_N}$ be as defined in $(\ref{28.08.2015A})$. 
For $X\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_N}$, if $\eta^X$ is a holomorphic eta quotient which is not factorizable on $\Gamma_0(N)$,
then either $X\in B_N\cdot[0,1)^{\mathbb{D}_N}$ or $X=B_N(\hspace{1.3pt}\underline{\hspace{5pt}}\hspace{1.3pt}\hspace{1.3pt},t)$ for some $t\in\mathbb{D}_N$.
     
\label{b2}

label: 9:58AM
title: Corollary
body_md:
For $X\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_N}$, if $\eta^X$ is a generic holomorphic eta quotient which is not factorizable on $\Gamma_0(N)$, then $X\in B_N\cdot[0,1)^{\mathbb{D}_N}$.
\label{9:58AM}
head: environment

label: 5:26AM
title: Lemma
body_md:
For $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{F}_N$ be as defined above. Then for $X\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_N}$, both the eta quotients $\eta^X$ and $\mathcal{F}_N/\eta^X$ are holomorphic if and and only if $X\in B_N\cdot [0,1]^{\mathbb{D}_N}$.
\label{5:26AM}
head: environment

label: 5:46AM
title: Corollary
body_md:
For $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $X\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_N}$, both the eta quotients $\eta^X$ and $\mathcal{F}_N/\eta^X$ are cuspidal if and and only if $X\in B_N\cdot (0,1)^{\mathbb{D}_N}$.
\label{5:46AM}
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
If $N$ has a unitary prime divisor and if the number of distinct prime divisors of $N$ is $r$, then 
$$\mathrm{d}(N)\leq 2(\log_2 N)^{r-1}.$$
               
Moreover, if $N$ is odd, 
                                  
then we have $\mathrm{d}(N)\leq 2(\log N)^{r-1}.$
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $N>1$ have $r$ distinct prime divisors,
                                                            
let $q$ be the least prime 
        
such that $q^2|N$, let $N':=N/\mathrm{rad}(N)$ and let 
$\rho:=\mathrm{rad}(N')$.
                                                                          
Then 
$$d(N)\leq 2(\log_2 N)^{r-1}+(\log_{\rho}N')^{\log_q\rho}.$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
From \eqref{6:08PM}, it follows that $\mathrm{d}(N)-2(\log_2 N)^{r-1}$ is bounded above 
by the quantity on the left hand side of the inequality
\begin{equation}
\displaystyle{\prod_{p|N'}(n_p-1)^{\log_q p}}\leq\left(\frac{\displaystyle{\sum_{p|N'}(n_p-1)\log_q p}}{\displaystyle{\sum_{p|N'}\log_q p}}\right)^{\log_{q}\mathrm{rad}(N')},
\nonumber\end{equation}
                           
which follows from the weighted AM-GM inequality\footnote{See 
              
also Theorem~1 in \cite{B8}}.
head: environment

label: 00:36AM
title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{S}_N$ be a special set of cusps of $\Gamma_0(N)$, let $B_N\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_N\times\mathbb{D}_N}$ be as defined in \eqref{28.08.2015A} and let $$X\in B_N\cdot[0,1)^{\mathbb{D}_N}\cap\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_N}$$ be such that 
$\eta^X$ is a holomorphic eta quotient on $\Gamma_0(N)$. Then $\eta^X$ is uniquely identified by its 
orders of vanishing at the cusp classes in $\mathcal{S}_N$.
\label{00:36AM}

title: Lemma
body_md:
Let 
$p$ be a prime, $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and 
let $f$ be an eta quotient on $\Gamma_0(p^n)$. Let $a:=24\cdot\operatorname{ord}_{1}(f;\Gamma_0(p^n))$ and $b:=24\cdot\operatorname{ord}_{1/p^n}(f;\Gamma_0(p^n))$. Then 
                                      
$$(p^{2-r_n}-1)\hspace{1.3pt}|\hspace{1.3pt}(a-b)$$
                                      
                                                
                           
where $r_n\in\{0,1\}$ is the residue of $n$ modulo 2.
\label{11:37PM}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_{p^n}}$ be such that $f=\eta^X$.
It follows from \eqref{28.04} and \eqref{12:47PM} that 
$$a=\sum_{j=0}^np^{n-j}X_{p^j}\text{ \ and \ }b=\sum_{j=0}^np^{j}X_{p^j}.$$
The claim now follows from the fact that $j$ and $n-j$ have the same parity 
                                                            
if and only if $n$ is even.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
For a prime $p$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $U_{p^n},V_{p^n}, U'_{p^n}$ and $V'_{p^n}\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_{p^n}\times\mathbb{D}_{p^n}}$ be the matrices as defined above. Let $B_{p^n}$ be as in $(\ref{equ1})$, $D_{p^n}$ be as in $(\ref{6:48AM})$
and let $I_{p^n}$ be the identity matrix in $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{D}_{p^n}\times\mathbb{D}_{p^n}}$. Then 
$$U_{p^n}U'_{p^n}=I_{p^n},\hspace{3pt} V_{p^n}V'_{p^n}=I_{p^n}\hspace{3pt}\text{ and } \hspace{3pt}D_{p^n}=U_{p^n}B_{p^n}V_{p^n}.$$
